segments.narration: Our goal is to find a path from A to F with the smallest total edge weight.
This three-edge route has total weight four plus five plus six, which is fifteen.
But this four-edge route totals thirteen. Fewer edges did not mean less weight, so we need a systematic way to find the minimum.
Each label is the best distance known so far. We begin with zero at A and infinity everywhere else.
Dijkstra always chooses the unfinalized node with the smallest tentative distance. Here, that node is A.
Removing the minimum finalizes A's distance. The separate current outline shows that we are now checking A's neighbors.
From A, the edge of weight four gives B a tentative distance of four.
The second edge gives C a tentative distance of two. That completes A's neighbor checks.
Two is smaller than four, so C is the next node selected.
Because every edge weight is non-negative, no later route through a farther node can reduce this minimum. C's distance can now be finalized.
Distances hold the best known costs. Predecessors remember the route, and the min-priority queue orders discovered, unfinalized nodes by distance.
The minimum item leaves the queue and moves to A. That removal finalizes A and makes it the current node.
Discovering a neighbor updates three records together: its distance, its predecessor, and its position in the queue.
The second neighbor receives the same coordinated update. The ordered queue now reveals which candidate is smaller.
The smallest queued distance leaves next. Its node becomes finalized and current for the next neighbor checks.
A tentative value can still improve. When a shorter route appears, its distance, predecessor, and queue position all change before finalization.
B currently costs four through A. We now ask whether reaching B through C is shorter.
Reaching C costs two, and the edge to B costs one more. The new candidate is three.
Three is less than four, so the route through C becomes the best known route to B.
B's tentative distance changes from four to three.
The shorter route came from C, so B's predecessor changes from A to C.
Finally, B's queue value becomes three and moves to its sorted position. A shorter route updates the distance, predecessor, and queue together.
For the full run, A starts at zero, every other distance starts at infinity, and A is the first queue item.
Removing the minimum finalizes A at distance zero and makes it current.
The edge to B discovers distance four, with A as B's predecessor.
The edge to C discovers distance two, with A as predecessor. C moves ahead of B in the queue, completing A's checks.
C has the smallest tentative distance, so it is finalized next at two.
The edge back to A needs no update because A is already finalized.
Through C, B costs two plus one, which is less than four. B improves to three, with C as its predecessor.
C also discovers D with tentative distance ten and predecessor C.
B is now the smallest candidate, so its distance three becomes final.
Reaching D through B costs eight, which improves the old value ten. D's predecessor changes to B.
B discovers E at distance ten with predecessor B. D remains first in the queue at eight.
Eight is the smallest tentative value, so D is finalized and becomes current.
Through D, the candidate for E is also ten. It is not smaller, so E's state does not change.
D discovers the target F at distance fourteen. But F is only tentative, so the search is not finished.
E's distance ten is smaller than F's fourteen, so E must be finalized first.
Through E, F costs thirteen, which improves fourteen. F's predecessor changes from D to E.
F is now the minimum. Removing it finalizes thirteen, so the search can stop.
The finalized shortest distance from A to F is thirteen.
Following predecessors backward leads from F to E, then B, then C, and finally A.
Reversing that chain gives A to C to B to E to F. Its weights are two plus one plus seven plus three, for a total of thirteen.
Dijkstra repeats three actions: extract the minimum, finalize its distance, and relax its edges.
This finalization rule requires every edge weight to be non-negative.
